title: About the project
standfirst: TRIAD co-creates and tests a framework that balances foundational competences, transversal competences and AI literacy in secondary schools and vocational education, with learner wellbeing built in.
context:
Across Europe, adolescents are growing up in a digital environment shaped by generative AI, smartphones and social media. These technologies transform how they learn, communicate and prepare for future careers. The tools enable creativity, personalisation and collaboration, but evidence on their impact on learning and wellbeing is fragmented and often lags behind practice.

TRIAD addresses this gap by co-creating and testing an integrated framework that balances foundational competences (literacy, numeracy, science), transversal competences (critical thinking, collaboration, metacognition) and AI and digital literacies, while embedding safeguards for cognitive, emotional and social wellbeing.

The project focuses on learners aged 12 to 18 in secondary schools and vocational education and training (VET), where competences must be consolidated and inequality risks peak.

challenges.title: Skill degradation and shallow learning
challenges.text: AI-driven skill degradation and shallow learning, with the risk of over-reliance and reduced originality.

challenges.title: Fragmented competence frameworks
challenges.text: Competence frameworks that are fragmented and lack operationalised pathways.

challenges.title: Uneven readiness and equity gaps
challenges.text: Uneven readiness and equity gaps that amplify socio-economic and digital divides.

challenges.title: Ambivalent evidence on wellbeing
challenges.text: Ambivalent evidence on adolescents' wellbeing in digitally enriched education.

approach: Through large-scale classroom pilots across Europe, combined with neuroscientific methods (EEG and fNIRS), TRIAD will identify when AI genuinely enhances learning rather than replacing it. Classroom scenarios will be validated across diverse contexts and enriched by input from SMEs and labour market actors.
results: The outputs are classroom-ready designs, developmental pathways for students and teachers, and actionable policy recommendations. They will enable schools to adopt AI responsibly, reduce inequalities and strengthen Europe's human capital and resilience, in line with the European Education Area 2030 and the Digital Education Action Plan.
